chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.

From Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O People, I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God, so turn straight to your Lord and seek His forgiveness.'
And he said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, has not made a place for polytheism in the body except as He makes water in a waterskin.'

key_terms.الشِّرْكِ: Polytheism or associating partners with God

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used in Shia hadith to describe the nature of polytheism in a person?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to establish the theological foundation of Tawhid as not merely a verbal declaration but an all-encompassing state of being, where Shirk infiltrates the core of one's faith like water saturating a waterskin. This metaphor underscores the Shia emphasis on the purity of belief (Aqidah) and serves as a critical criterion for distinguishing true monotheism from superficial adherence, a key theme in the validation of the Imams' teachings.
